lblName: Pop-up attack: run in low, pull up at the pull-up point (PUP), climb, roll in at the top and dive onto the target. The Mode knob to the right picks what the right half of the page shows.
lblSelections: Selections: the target steerpoint (TGT STPT), the reference the DED uses (VIP or VRP), the profile type and the bomb.
lblProfName: Profile: a drawing of the attack you chose, and the map around the target with every point of it.
lblInputPanel: Input: the sliders that shape the attack (heading, ingress height, speed, dive angle, release height, tracking time, G). Every figure on the page follows them.
lblTurnPanel: Turn Data: the pull-up and roll-in worked out from your sliders: offset angle, pull heading, climb, angle off and the pulldown height.
lblSpeedExpl: The release height and dive angle the TAS and ground speed beside it are worked out for: your Release Height and Dive Angle sliders.
lblDeliveryMode: The bombing mode to use in the jet for this attack: CCIP (the HUD shows where the bombs will hit; release when it is on the target) or DTOS (dive toss: designate the target, hold the pickle button, the jet releases).
pnlBlocked_3: VIP is blocked: the IP STPT has no position in this mission. Pick another IP STPT, or press IP STPT at the VRP. The page plans from the VRP.
lblDEDRef: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblDED_Ref_VRP: VRP: the DED lines are measured from the target (TGT-TO-VRP, TGT-TO-PUP), and the run-in starts at the VRP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
lblDED_Ref_VIP: VIP: the DED lines are measured from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another): VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP. VRP needs no IP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
pnlDED_Ref_Down: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblPUPnmName: The same range in nautical miles.
lblPUPnm: The same range in nautical miles.
lblVRPnmName: The same range in nautical miles.
lblVIPnm: The same range in nautical miles.
lblDEDData: The jet's DED (data entry display) nav-offset pages as they will read after Save to DTC: true bearings, ranges in feet, ELEVs in feet above sea level (0 = ground level). Every ELEV can be typed: click or tap its figure.
lblTargetHUDval: YES (green) when at release the target is under 260 mils (about 15°) below your flight path, so it is still in the HUD; NO (red) when it is further down.
lblTargetHUD: YES (green) when at release the target is under 260 mils (about 15°) below your flight path, so it is still in the HUD; NO (red) when it is further down.
lblOA2nmName: The same range in nautical miles.
lblOA1nmName: The same range in nautical miles.
lblOA1nm: The same range in nautical miles.
lblOA2nm: The same range in nautical miles.
pnlDED_Ref_Up: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
pnlDEDpup: VIP-TO-PUP or TGT-TO-PUP: the pull-up point, where you pull up off the run-in, by true bearing, range in feet and ELEV from the IP (VIP) or the target (VRP).
lblPUPelv: This line's ELEV, in feet above sea level; 0 means ground level wherever the point is. A dotted frame is the page's own figure: click or tap to type yours (the frame turns solid), clear it to go back. Save to DTC writes what shows.
pnlDEDOA1: DEST OA1: offset aimpoint 1, a point the jet marks for you: the pull-down point where you roll in, at the Pulldown height. Range and true bearing from the IP STPT (VIP) or the TGT STPT (VRP): offsets always hang on a steerpoint.
lblOA1elv: This line's ELEV, in feet above sea level; 0 means ground level wherever the point is. A dotted frame is the page's own figure: click or tap to type yours (the frame turns solid), clear it to go back. Save to DTC writes what shows.
pnlDEDOA2: DEST OA2: offset aimpoint 2: on the aim-off point past the target with Place OA2 at the Aim Off Point checked, else on OA1. Range and true bearing from the IP STPT (VIP) or the TGT STPT (VRP): offsets always hang on a steerpoint.
lblOA2elv: This line's ELEV, in feet above sea level; 0 means ground level wherever the point is. A dotted frame is the page's own figure: click or tap to type yours (the frame turns solid), clear it to go back. Save to DTC writes what shows.
pnlDEDvip: VIP-TO-TGT (VIP reference): true bearing and range in feet from the IP to the target. TGT-TO-VRP (VRP): from the target to the VRP, where the run-in starts. The number is the steerpoint the line hangs on: the IP STPT for VIP, the TGT STPT for VRP.
lblVIPelv: This line's ELEV, in feet above sea level; 0 means ground level wherever the point is. A dotted frame is the page's own figure: click or tap to type yours (the frame turns solid), clear it to go back. Save to DTC writes what shows.
pnlBlocked_1: VIP is blocked: the IP STPT has no position in this mission. Pick another IP STPT, or press IP STPT at the VRP. The page plans from the VRP.
lblReference: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblRefDown: VRP: the DED lines are measured from the target (TGT-TO-VRP, TGT-TO-PUP), and the run-in starts at the VRP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
lblRefUp: VIP: the DED lines are measured from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another): VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP. VRP needs no IP. Click the knob beside it to choose it.
lblIP_elv: The altitude the IP's steerpoint carries in the mission, in feet: for a route point, the height planned there, not the ground.
lblIP_E: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only). Hidden in VRP mode, and when that steerpoint has no position (then there is no IP).
lblIP_N: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only). Hidden in VRP mode, and when that steerpoint has no position (then there is no IP).
lblTGT_elv: Ground under the target, feet above sea level: what you typed, else BMS's terrain, else your cartridge's target point (0 if none is known). Click or tap the framed figure to type yours; clear it to go back. Every ELEV stands on it.
lblTGT_E: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position. Hidden while the theater is not known or the steerpoint has no position.
lblTGT_EW: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position. Hidden while the theater is not known or the steerpoint has no position.
lblTGT_NS: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position. Hidden while the theater is not known or the steerpoint has no position.
btnIpAtVrp: IP STPT at the VRP (VRP mode): puts a steerpoint on the VRP and plans this attack as VIP from it, after one question. Finish the Input Panel first: the steerpoint stays where it is placed, so a later change moves the attack but not the steerpoint. Save to DTC writes it; delete it on DTC → STPT (Change on its row, Clear, Apply). In VIP mode it moves the IP STPT it created.
numIPpoint: VIP only: the steerpoint you overfly as the visual initial point — the jet's VIP (LIST 3). The jet steers to it; VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP and the offsets are measured from it. It follows the target (TGT STPT − 1) until you pick another. Shown in VIP mode, and while VIP is blocked so an IP can be picked.
lblIPpoint: VIP only: the steerpoint you overfly as the visual initial point — the jet's VIP (LIST 3). The jet steers to it; VIP-TO-TGT, VIP-TO-PUP and the offsets are measured from it. It follows the target (TGT STPT − 1) until you pick another. Shown in VIP mode, and while VIP is blocked so an IP can be picked.
lblIPelv: The altitude the IP's steerpoint carries in the mission, in feet: for a route point, the height planned there, not the ground.
lblTGTelv: Ground under the target, feet above sea level: what you typed, else BMS's terrain, else your cartridge's target point (0 if none is known). Click or tap the framed figure to type yours; clear it to go back. Every ELEV stands on it.
lblIPelv2: The altitude the IP's steerpoint carries in the mission, in feet: for a route point, the height planned there, not the ground.
lblTGTelv2: Ground under the target, feet above sea level: what you typed, else BMS's terrain, else your cartridge's target point (0 if none is known). Click or tap the framed figure to type yours; clear it to go back. Every ELEV stands on it.
lblIP_EW: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only). Hidden in VRP mode, and when that steerpoint has no position (then there is no IP).
lblIP_NS: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only). Hidden in VRP mode, and when that steerpoint has no position (then there is no IP).
numWaypoint: TGT STPT: the steerpoint the attack is planned on, 1 to 25; the IP is the one before it unless you pick another in IP STPT (VIP only). A new mission or flight sets it once to your first strike steerpoint; after that it is yours.
lblWaypoint: TGT STPT: the steerpoint the attack is planned on, 1 to 25; the IP is the one before it unless you pick another in IP STPT (VIP only). A new mission or flight sets it once to your first strike steerpoint; after that it is yours.
lblNewCoordinate: The IP's latitude and longitude: the IP STPT (VIP only). Hidden in VRP mode, and when that steerpoint has no position (then there is no IP).
lblTarget: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position. Hidden while the theater is not known or the steerpoint has no position.
lblTGT_N: The target's latitude and longitude (degrees, minutes), from the TGT STPT's position. Hidden while the theater is not known or the steerpoint has no position.
pnlHighDrag: High Drag: a retarded bomb (fins or a ballute open after release): it falls shorter and steeper than a slick one. Click the Bomb knob to choose it.
pnlLowDrag: Low Drag: a slick bomb, which carries further after release. Click the Bomb knob to choose it.
lblLowDrag: Low Drag: a slick bomb, which carries further after release. Click the Bomb knob to choose it.
lblHighDrag: High Drag: a retarded bomb (fins or a ballute open after release): it falls shorter and steeper than a slick one. Click the Bomb knob to choose it.
lblBomb: Bomb knob: Low Drag for a slick bomb (Mk-82 and alike), High Drag for a retarded one (Snakeye fins or an AIR ballute). It sets the bomb's range. Click the knob to turn it.
lblProfile: Profile knob: Type 1 runs in from the VRP pointed at the target and turns off as you pull up; Type 2 runs in on the pull heading, the target off to one side. Click the knob to turn it.
lblMAT: Type 2: run in on the pull heading with the target off to one side, and pull straight up at the PUP. Click the Profile knob to choose it.
lblLAT: Type 1: run in from the VRP pointed at the target, and turn off by the Offset Angle as you pull up at the PUP. Click the Profile knob to choose it.
pnlBomb_Up: Bomb knob: Low Drag for a slick bomb (Mk-82 and alike), High Drag for a retarded one (Snakeye fins or an AIR ballute). It sets the bomb's range. Click the knob to turn it.
pnlProfile_Up: Profile knob: Type 1 runs in from the VRP pointed at the target and turns off as you pull up; Type 2 runs in on the pull heading, the target off to one side. Click the knob to turn it.
pnlBomb_Down: Bomb knob: Low Drag for a slick bomb (Mk-82 and alike), High Drag for a retarded one (Snakeye fins or an AIR ballute). It sets the bomb's range. Click the knob to turn it.
pnlProfile_Down: Profile knob: Type 1 runs in from the VRP pointed at the target and turns off as you pull up; Type 2 runs in on the pull heading, the target off to one side. Click the knob to turn it.
pnlRefUp: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
pnlRefDown: Reference knob: VIP (visual initial point) measures the DED lines from the IP STPT (the steerpoint before the target unless you pick another); VRP (visual reference point) from the target itself. Click the knob to turn it to the other. VIP needs an IP with a position; VRP needs no IP.
lblBombTime: Bomb Fall Time: seconds from release to impact, for the bomb, the speed, the dive angle and the release height.
lblBombFallTime: Bomb Fall Time: seconds from release to impact, for the bomb, the speed, the dive angle and the release height.
lblGS: Ground speed in the dive, in knots: the TAS times the cosine of the dive angle. It gives the ground covered while tracking.
lblGsVal: Ground speed in the dive, in knots: the TAS times the cosine of the dive angle. It gives the ground covered while tracking.
lblE: Sets the attack heading to east, 90°.
lblS: Sets the attack heading to south, 180°.
lblW: Sets the attack heading to west, 270°.
lblN360: Sets the attack heading to north, 360°.
lblN: Sets the attack heading to north, 0°.
lblTurnVal: Turn To Target: which way you turn in toward the target after the pull-up, left or right. It sets the side the pull-up point and OA1 lie on, and the Pull Heading.
trbTurn: Turn To Target: which way you turn in toward the target after the pull-up, left or right. It sets the side the pull-up point and OA1 lie on, and the Pull Heading.
lblVrpToPupVal: VRP to PUP dist: how far before the pull-up point the VRP lies on the run-in, 1 to 5 nm. Shown with the VRP reference only; with VIP the run is measured from the IP.
trbVrpToPup: VRP to PUP dist: how far before the pull-up point the VRP lies on the run-in, 1 to 5 nm. Shown with the VRP reference only; with VIP the run is measured from the IP.
lblAttackHdgVal: Attack heading: your heading in the dive at the target, 0 to 360° true. Click N, E, S or W under the slider for 0, 90, 180 or 270. Every point is laid out from it.
trbHeading: Attack heading: your heading in the dive at the target, 0 to 360° true. Click N, E, S or W under the slider for 0, 90, 180 or 270. Every point is laid out from it.
lblGVal: Pulling G's: the G of your pull-up and roll-in, 2.0 to 6.0 in tenths. It sets the turn radius, and so where the pull-up point and OA1 lie.
trbG: Pulling G's: the G of your pull-up and roll-in, 2.0 to 6.0 in tenths. It sets the turn radius, and so where the pull-up point and OA1 lie.
lblTrackingTimeVal: Tracking Time: seconds you track the target wings level in the dive before release, 1 to 10 (1 to 5 from a 5,000 ft release height up). More time moves the roll-in further out.
trbTrackingTime: Tracking Time: seconds you track the target wings level in the dive before release, 1 to 10 (1 to 5 from a 5,000 ft release height up). More time moves the roll-in further out.
lblCasVal: Speed: your calibrated airspeed in the dive and at release, 300 to 550 kts. Through the true airspeed it sets the bomb range, the turn radius and every distance on the DED.
trbSpeed: Speed: your calibrated airspeed in the dive and at release, 300 to 550 kts. Through the true airspeed it sets the bomb range, the turn radius and every distance on the DED.
lblDiveAngleVal: Dive Angle: the dive at release, 10 to 45°. On a multiple of 5 it also sets the Release Height range (steeper dives release higher). The climb after the pull-up follows it.
trbDiveAngle: Dive Angle: the dive at release, 10 to 45°. On a multiple of 5 it also sets the Release Height range (steeper dives release higher). The climb after the pull-up follows it.
lblIngressHeightVal: Ingress Alt: your height above the target's ground on the run-in to the pull-up, 100 to 500 ft. The DED's ELEVs add the ground under the target, so they read feet above sea level.
trbIngressHeight: Ingress Alt: your height above the target's ground on the run-in to the pull-up, 100 to 500 ft. The DED's ELEVs add the ground under the target, so they read feet above sea level.
lblReleaseHeightVal: Release Height: feet above the target at release. Its range follows the dive angle: 300 to 4,000 ft at 10°, up to 4,000 to 10,000 ft at 45°.
trbReleaseHeight: Release Height: feet above the target at release. Its range follows the dive angle: 300 to 4,000 ft at 10°, up to 4,000 to 10,000 ft at 45°.
chbOA2: Checked: OA2 goes on the aim-off point, the Aim Off Dist past the target along the attack heading, where your dive line meets the ground. Unchecked: OA2 repeats OA1's position at the ingress altitude, as WDP writes it; the maps draw OA1 only.
lblTASval: True airspeed at the release height for your Speed, in knots.
lblTAS: True airspeed at the release height for your Speed, in knots.
lblAODval: Aim Off Dist: feet past the target where the dive line from the release point meets the ground. Hold the flight path marker there in the dive; the bomb falls short onto the target.
lblAOD: Aim Off Dist: feet past the target where the dive line from the release point meets the ground. Hold the flight path marker there in the dive; the bomb falls short onto the target.
lblAttackHdg: Attack heading: your heading in the dive at the target, 0 to 360° true. Click N, E, S or W under the slider for 0, 90, 180 or 270. Every point is laid out from it.
lblVRPtoPUPdist: VRP to PUP dist: how far before the pull-up point the VRP lies on the run-in, 1 to 5 nm. Shown with the VRP reference only; with VIP the run is measured from the IP.
lblIngressAlt: Ingress Alt: your height above the target's ground on the run-in to the pull-up, 100 to 500 ft. The DED's ELEVs add the ground under the target, so they read feet above sea level.
lblDiveAngle: Dive Angle: the dive at release, 10 to 45°. On a multiple of 5 it also sets the Release Height range (steeper dives release higher). The climb after the pull-up follows it.
lblSpeed: Speed: your calibrated airspeed in the dive and at release, 300 to 550 kts. Through the true airspeed it sets the bomb range, the turn radius and every distance on the DED.
lblReleaseHeight: Release Height: feet above the target at release. Its range follows the dive angle: 300 to 4,000 ft at 10°, up to 4,000 to 10,000 ft at 45°.
lblTrackingTime: Tracking Time: seconds you track the target wings level in the dive before release, 1 to 10 (1 to 5 from a 5,000 ft release height up). More time moves the roll-in further out.
lblPullingGs: Pulling G's: the G of your pull-up and roll-in, 2.0 to 6.0 in tenths. It sets the turn radius, and so where the pull-up point and OA1 lie.
lblTurnToTarget: Turn To Target: which way you turn in toward the target after the pull-up, left or right. It sets the side the pull-up point and OA1 lie on, and the Pull Heading.
chbShowPPTNr: Writes each threat's PPT number beside its ring on the map.
chbShowPPT: Draws your cartridge's pre-planned threats (PPTs) on the map, each with its range as a red ring.
lblZoomText: Zoom: how much of the theater the map shows around the target, from about 8 nm across (left, 100%) to about 80 nm (right, 0%).
trbZoom: Zoom: how much of the theater the map shows around the target, from about 8 nm across (left, 100%) to about 80 nm (right, 0%).
pnlLabelcover: The map's key: the target a red square, the VIP a blue square or the VRP a blue circle, the pull-up point (PUP) a magenta ring, OA1 and OA2 green triangles; the white line is the run-in the jet flies, dotted past the target to OA2.
btnSaveMap: Saves this map as a JPEG on the BMS PC: a Save window opens on the SavedMaps folder (WDP's own, when WDP is on the PC), named PopUp.jpg.
lblZoom: Zoom: how much of the theater the map shows around the target, from about 8 nm across (left, 100%) to about 80 nm (right, 0%).
lblType2_2: Type 2: run in on the pull heading with the target off to one side, and pull straight up at the PUP. Click the Profile knob to choose it.
lblProf: Profile knob: Type 1 runs in from the VRP pointed at the target and turns off as you pull up; Type 2 runs in on the pull heading, the target off to one side. Click the knob to turn it.
picProfile: Falcas's drawing of the profile you chose: the reference, Type 1 or 2, the turn direction and where OA2 goes.
lblType1_2: Type 1: run in from the VRP pointed at the target, and turn off by the Offset Angle as you pull up at the PUP. Click the Profile knob to choose it.
picSatView: The attack drawn on the theater map round the target, as every map draws it: target red square, VIP blue square or VRP blue circle, PUP magenta ring, OA1 and OA2 green triangles, the run-in line; your route with its numbers, threats in red rings; the foot names the attack and the TGT STPT.
pnlProfile2_Up: Profile knob: Type 1 runs in from the VRP pointed at the target and turns off as you pull up; Type 2 runs in on the pull heading, the target off to one side. Click the knob to turn it.
pnlProfile2_Down: Profile knob: Type 1 runs in from the VRP pointed at the target and turns off as you pull up; Type 2 runs in on the pull heading, the target off to one side. Click the knob to turn it.
lblMode: Mode knob: Selections (target and choices), Profile (drawing and map) or DED Data (the figures for the jet). A click on it turns it one step on; right-click turns it back.
lblShowProfile: Turns the Mode knob straight to Profile: the drawing of the attack and the map around the target.
lblHideSelections: Turns the Mode knob straight to Selections: the target steerpoint, the reference, the profile type and the bomb.
lblShowSelections: Turns the Mode knob straight to DED Data: the figures for the jet's DED, and whether the target shows in the HUD.
pnlSelections_Up: Mode knob: Selections (target and choices), Profile (drawing and map) or DED Data (the figures for the jet). A click on it turns it one step on; right-click turns it back.
pnlSelections_Middle: Mode knob: Selections (target and choices), Profile (drawing and map) or DED Data (the figures for the jet). A click on it turns it one step on; right-click turns it back.
pnlSelections_Down: Mode knob: Selections (target and choices), Profile (drawing and map) or DED Data (the figures for the jet). A click on it turns it one step on; right-click turns it back.
btnSaveDTC: Writes the four DED lines of the reference in use (VIP or VRP, PUP, OA1, OA2) into your cartridge's nav offsets and saves the cartridge now. The other reference's lines are cleared: VIP and VRP cannot be used together. Once saved, the DataCard's Delivery section becomes this attack, so the card and the cartridge agree; a save that fails leaves the card as it was.
lblOffsetAngleVal: Offset Angle: at the pull-up point, the angle between the line to the target and your pull heading, in degrees.
lblOffsetAngle: Offset Angle: at the pull-up point, the angle between the line to the target and your pull heading, in degrees.
lblAngleOffVal: Angle Off: how far you turn from the pull heading onto the attack heading as you roll in, in degrees: twice the climb angle.
lblAngleOff: Angle Off: how far you turn from the pull heading onto the attack heading as you roll in, in degrees: twice the climb angle.
lblPulldownAltVal: Pulldown height: where you roll in and pull down into the dive (the apex), feet above sea level with the ground under the target. OA1 carries it as its ELEV.
lblClimbAngleVal: Climb Angle: your climb after the pull-up, in degrees: the dive angle + 5° for dives up to 15°, + 10° above.
lblPullHeadingVal: Pull Heading: the heading you climb on after the pull-up: the attack heading turned by the Angle Off, away from the side you turn in to.
lblPulldownAlt: Pulldown height: where you roll in and pull down into the dive (the apex), feet above sea level with the ground under the target. OA1 carries it as its ELEV.
lblClimbAngle: Climb Angle: your climb after the pull-up, in degrees: the dive angle + 5° for dives up to 15°, + 10° above.
lblPullHeading: Pull Heading: the heading you climb on after the pull-up: the attack heading turned by the Angle Off, away from the side you turn in to.
